prompt: Reinforcement learning from scratch as a learning path: bandits, MDPs and returns, Bellman equations, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo vs TD, SARSA and Q-learning, DQN, policy gradients, actor-critic and GAE, TRPO/PPO, then bridges to model-based RL and RL for LLMs. Teaching first, papers second; freedom to improve the flow.
reader_background: ML engineer at a computer-vision company; knows deep learning basics; new to RL. Explain from scratch.
mode: course: a learning path, not a literature survey and not a named-paper list. No arXiv scan or map chapter.

sources_plan.classical_core: Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed. (2018; RLbook2020.pdf at incompleteideas.net). Non-arXiv primary source for the bandit to Q-learning chapters; most figures there are toy or computed, not sourced.
non_arxiv_primary: Sutton 1988, Learning to predict by the methods of temporal differences (TD)
Sutton, McAllester, Singh, Mansour 2000 (policy gradient theorem, NeurIPS 1999)
Mnih et al. 2015, Nature (DQN, human-level control)

cross_links.world-models: Dreamer, MuZero and world models: the model-based chapter is a short bridge plus link, not a re-explanation
cross_links.post-training: RLHF with PPO, DPO, GRPO and reasoning RL: the LLM chapter is a short bridge plus link

design_decisions.spine: RL differs from supervised learning in three ways: exploration, delayed credit, and data that the policy itself generates. Each chapter fixes part of one.
design_decisions.live_vs_recorded: Tabular algorithms (bandits, DP sweeps, MC/TD, SARSA/Q-learning, Dyna, small REINFORCE) run live in the page with a seeded rng. DQN and PPO on CartPole are trained offline in NumPy (build/sim/ -> notes/sim-*.txt) and shown as a scrubber, badge Computed.
design_decisions.plants: n-step returns in MC vs TD (for GAE); importance sampling and on/off-policy at SARSA vs Q-learning (for the PPO ratio and the replay buffer)
